content.intro: Print a Dutch Blitz score sheet for playing to 75, or keep score on your phone. The plus and minus scoring is on this page.
howToUse: Write each player's name at the top of a column. A hand ends the moment a player empties their Blitz pile and calls out Blitz.

Sort the Dutch piles in the middle by the back of each card. Every player scores 1 point for each of their cards in the Dutch piles and loses 2 points for each card still in their Blitz pile. Write the result for each player in the hand's row; it can be negative.
The first player to reach 75 points wins. If two players pass 75 in the same hand, the higher total wins; online, the sheet waits until every score for that hand is in.

faqs.q: How do you score Dutch Blitz?
faqs.a: When someone calls Blitz, each player scores 1 point for every one of their cards in the Dutch piles in the middle and loses 2 points for every card left in their Blitz pile.

faqs.q: How many points do you need to win Dutch Blitz?
faqs.a: 75. The first player to reach 75 points at the end of a hand wins the game.

faqs.q: Can you get a negative score in Dutch Blitz?
faqs.a: Yes. If you have few cards in the middle and many left in your Blitz pile, your score for the hand is negative and comes off your total.

faqs.q: How do you know whose cards are in the Dutch piles?
faqs.a: Each player's deck has its own symbol on the back: a pump, carriage, plow or bucket. Sort the piles by the backs and count each player's cards.

faqs.q: How many cards are in the Blitz pile?
faqs.a: Ten, dealt face down with the top card turned up. Emptying it ends the hand.

faqs.q: How many people can play Dutch Blitz?
faqs.a: Two to four with the basic set, and up to eight with an expansion pack.
